payload.claim: Criterion 3 requires 'the lower id as a string' to win the stack-base tie-break when two parents qualify, but `test_a_stack_order_stacks_on_one_earlier_pull_request_and_refuses_a_spec_naming_another` creates every qualifying parent's task in the same order as the alphabetical id order it also wants to test (e.g. `TB-A1`'s task is created before `TB-B1`'s, `TB-A3` before `TB-B3`), so the lower spec id always also has the lower `task_id`. A wrong version that breaks the tie by earliest `task_id` instead of lowest spec-id string produces the identical chosen stack base and reason text in every arrangement this witness runs, so the witness cannot tell the two implementations apart.
